documents.title: Telephone Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called for metoprolol refill (sent, 90 days). Also wanted the doctor to know he quit cigarettes right after New Year's -- cold turkey, about 4 weeks now. Some irritability, chewing gum, no patches. Congratulated; offered NRT if cravings get bad, he declined. Missed Dec visit: rebooked for March.

PCP: Great news. Updated smoking status. Keep the March appt.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
68M, routine f/u (cancelled in March).

HPI: His main agenda today is his blood pressure -- he'd like to try a natural route rather than add anything. Not keen on more pills. Denies chest pain, headaches, lightheadedness. Has not needed nitro since winter. Off cigarettes since January, about 5 months, still chewing gum. Beer still 2-3 most nights. Cooks for himself; honest that it's mostly cold cuts, hot dogs, boxed meals.

Meds reviewed: lisinopril 10, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succinate 50, ASA 81, atorvastatin 40, NTG prn. Says he takes the lisinopril; keeps all bottles on the kitchen counter.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: lives alone. 40 pk-yr history, former smoker as of 1/2024.

Objective: BP 150/92, P 82, RR 16, T 98.7 F. BMI 33.
Gen: comfortable, obese. CV: regular, no murmur, no gallop heard. Lungs: clear. Ext: no edema.

Assessment / plan:
1. Hypertension -- above goal. He wants to work on it himself first: walk 20-30 min most days, cut processed meats and canned soups (sodium), DASH handout, try to halve the beer. No medication change today per his preference; recheck in about 3 months, bring home log.
2. Obesity, BMI 33 -- added to problem list; diet as above.
3. CAD / stable angina -- quiet. Continue ASA, statin, beta blocker.
4. Former smoker -- well done; LDCT due again in November.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group -- annual follow-up, seen 2024-07-16.

Coronary artery disease with chronic stable angina. He reports no chest discomfort over recent months and has not used nitroglycerin. He stopped smoking this year, which we strongly support. No dyspnea or palpitations reported.
Exam: regular rhythm, no murmur, clear lungs, no edema.
Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed. Allergies: none known.
Plan: no changes. Return one year.

Cardiology

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST FOR LUNG CANCER SCREENING
Comparison: 2023-11-07, 2022-11-08.
Smoking history: 40 pack-years, quit 2024.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear. No pleural effusion. Central airways patent. Heart size within normal limits. No lymphadenopathy. Limited upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS category 1: negative. Recommend continued annual screening.

conditions.label: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 78. Normal axis. Normal intervals. Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. No acute ST-segment changes.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy.

reports.text:
TRANSTHORACIC ECHOCARDIOGRAM
Indication: dyspnea, hypertension.
Left ventricle: normal cavity size, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Normal wall motion. LVEF 55-60% (visual estimate). Mitral inflow and tissue Doppler show an impaired relaxation pattern.
Right ventricle: normal size and function.
Valves: no significant stenosis or regurgitation.
Pericardium: no effusion.
reports.conclusion: Preserved LV systolic function, LVEF 55-60%. Concentric LVH with impaired relaxation. Normal RV. No significant valve disease.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary -- Cardiology
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 2025-02-05, discharged 2025-02-07.

Principal diagnosis: acute hypertensive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure), preserved ejection fraction.

History: 69-year-old man with hypertension, coronary artery disease with chronic stable angina and obesity, admitted with exertional breathlessness progressing over several months and occasional episodes of waking short of breath at night. He acknowledged taking his antihypertensives irregularly. Hydrochlorothiazide is his main stated BP drug.

On arrival: BP 160/90, HR 78, BMI 32. Presystolic (S4) gallop at the apex, accentuated in the left lateral decubitus position. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema.

Labs: Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 1.1, fasting glucose 98. Total cholesterol 210, LDL 140, HDL 40.
ECG: sinus rhythm, left ventricular hypertrophy.
Echo 2/6: LVEF 55-60%, concentric LVH, impaired relaxation, normal RV, no significant valvular disease.

Hospital course: Monitored on telemetry without arrhythmia. Home antihypertensives given daily under observation with improvement in BP and in breathing on ward ambulation. Extensive teaching on taking medications every day, sodium restriction and daily weights.

Discharge medications (unchanged): lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL prn chest pain.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit about a year ago; 2-3 beers nightly; retired long-haul truck driver; lives alone.
Family: father MI at 64; mother hypertension and stroke; brother type 2 diabetes.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; cardiology clinic in 6 weeks.

Hospital medicine / cardiology

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after receiving discharge summary. Home since Friday, says breathing 'much better.' Has all six meds at home, no changes made at discharge. Reviewed: take them every morning, use a pill box, weigh daily before breakfast, call for gain of 3 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week or worse breathing. No bathroom scale -- will buy one. TCM visit booked 2/13.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 6 days after discharge (admitted 2/5-2/7, cardiology service, acute hypertensive HF with preserved EF). Discharge summary and echo reviewed.

He is breathing better. Walks to the mailbox and around the block without stopping. Sleeps flat, no waking up short of breath since he got home. No chest pain. Bought a scale, weights steady over 3 days. Admits that before the admission he went days at a time without his pills -- 'I'd take them when I remembered.' Now using a weekly pill organizer his daughter set up.

Meds reconciled: no changes at discharge. Lisinopril 10, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succ 50, ASA 81, atorvastatin 40, NTG prn.

Exam: BP lower than hospital, still above goal. No JVD. Heart regular, S4 not appreciated today. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Heart failure with preserved EF, hypertensive heart disease -- added to problem list. Euvolemic. Daily weights, 2 g sodium, limit beer (also fluid). Call parameters reviewed.
2. HTN -- adherence was the main issue; continue regimen, recheck.
3. CAD -- no angina.
BMP today. Cardiology clinic 6 wks. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Kidney and potassium check
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and potassium are normal. Keep up the daily weights and the pill box.

documents.title: Cardiology Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group -- clinic visit 2025-03-19, post-hospital follow-up.

Dear colleague,
We saw Mr. Sheehan six weeks after his admission for hypertensive heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (LVEF 55-60%, concentric LVH). His exertional breathlessness has improved and he has had no further nocturnal episodes. He is taking his medications daily with a pill organizer.

BP 142/86, HR 70. Lungs clear, no peripheral edema, no JVD.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, SL nitroglycerin prn. NKDA.

Impression: HFpEF due to hypertensive heart disease, clinically improved; stable angina, quiet. No medication changes today. Continue sodium restriction and daily weights.
Return in 6 months.

Cardiology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3-month f/u, HFpEF/HTN/CAD. Cardiology letter from March reviewed.

Feels well. Walking most days, gardening. No orthopnea or PND; sleeps on one pillow. No chest pain. Home weights steady (scale reads about 220). Pill organizer working, he thinks he's missed 2 doses in a month. Still has 2 beers most nights, down from 3. Not smoking.

Exam: BP best we've seen. Neck veins flat. Regular, no gallop. Lungs clear to bases. No pedal edema.

A/P:
- HFpEF / hypertensive heart disease: compensated. Continue regimen, sodium limits, daily weights.
- HTN: improved with adherence.
- CAD/angina: quiet.
- Former smoker: LDCT due November.
BMP, lipids today. RTC 3 months, AWV in fall with flu shot.
